cohort: Women aged 15-54 years with asthma who gave birth in the US between 2000 and 2018, identified through the National Inpatient Sample
finding: The study found that asthma prevalence during delivery hospitalizations increased significantly from 2000 to 2018 and was associated with increased risk of various adverse maternal outcomes, including severe maternal morbidity, preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, and preterm delivery.
mod_finding: Asthma was associated with cesarean delivery (aOR 1.16, 95% CI 1.15-1.18).
